scene.note: Kofi's text arrives as one block, and the elements you choose turn it into an outline and short sections a visitor can scan.

steps.note: Kofi's text has three section titles, but they sit inside the paragraph like any other words.
Turn each title into a heading one level below the studio name, with its words unchanged.
The headings form the page's outline, and no level is skipped on the way down.
Under the titles there are six pieces of text, each one idea.
Give each piece its own paragraph, with the headings standing between them.
The browser leaves space between paragraphs, so the block turns into short sections.
One line is a warning about clothes, and one line leans on the word Saturday.
Mark the warning as important and the one word as stressed, with the elements that carry meaning.
The browser shows them in bold and italics, and a screen reader knows they matter.
On the page the three parts of the address run together on one line.
Keep the address in one paragraph of its own and break the line after the street and the town.
Now the address reads the way it would on an envelope.
